title: Text units and vocabulary IDs
description: A quick reference for Chapter 1's text units, fixed vocabulary, and decoding limit.

terms.definition: An eight-bit storage unit in UTF-8 text. One Unicode scalar value may occupy several bytes.
A Unicode code point other than a surrogate code point. Rust char represents one scalar, and this demo assigns one token position to each input scalar.
A fixed table associating represented units with IDs. Chapter 1 uses seven known scalars from cat кот; later byte-level BPE uses a separate table and ID namespace.
An integer label for a vocabulary entry, distinct from a text position, Unicode value, or semantic magnitude. Later it selects an embedding-table row.
The demo's reserved ID 0, decoded as <UNK>. All absent scalars share this ID and lose their identities; the later byte tokenizer instead represents every input byte.
Encoding followed by decoding that recovers the original text. This scalar demo guarantees it only when every input scalar is in the fixed vocabulary.
A unit that approximates a character as a reader perceives it and can contain several Unicode scalars. The scalar demo does not segment grapheme clusters.
A tokenizer using units smaller than whole words so known units can compose new forms. The later byte-level BPE tokenizer learns units spanning adjacent bytes.
